community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "Whiplash"] Whiplash very effectively demonstrates my problems with Dane Clark as an actor.* I've never really bought into the idea that he plays an "everyman" role — more often than not, he's got an off-putting cockiness to him, and comes across as a guy totally unaware of his own obnoxiousness who assumes everyone thinks he's charming. And that's the problem — the movies in which he stars usually reflect that inaccurate assumption, which creates an intense disconnect with the viewer (by which I mean "me"). community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "Whiplash"] This had potential but was kind of a mess. A mixture of noir/love story/boxing drama, Warner Brothers threw together plot elements from lots of similar films. It made for a complicated story that doesn't quite work. I watched it primarily for the cast (Dane Clark, Alexis Smith, Zachary Scott, Eve Arden) but the plot ultimately worked against them.Clark is a Mike Gordon, a California coastal artist. community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "Whiplash"] One of those natural B's shakily promoted to an A so that a bunch of really-too-good-for-this contract players could be kept laboring between higher-quality projects, but executed with such baseline studio brio that it's more engrossing than it ought to be. My semi-regular reminder that I under-value Dane Clark, though seeing Deep Valley, Moonrise and Gunman in the Streets should have settled that long ago. community_snippets.title: Wikipedia: Whiplash (2014 film)
community_snippets.snippet:
[Wikipedia Synopsis] Whiplash is a 2014 American independent psychological drama film written and directed by Damien Chazelle, and starring Miles Teller, J. K. Simmons, and Paul Reiser. It focuses on an ambitious music student and aspiring jazz drummer (Teller), who is pushed to his limit by his abusive instructor (Simmons).
The film was produced by Bold Films, Blumhouse Productions, and Right of Way Films. Sony Pictures acquired distribution rights for most of the world, releasing the film under Sony Pictures Classics in North America, Germany, and Australia, and Stage 6 Films in the UK, Scandinavia, Benelux, Eastern Europe (excluding the CIS), Greece, South Africa, Spain, Italy, Portugal and Latin America.
Chazelle completed the script in 2013, drawing upon his experiences in a "very competitive" jazz band in high school. Soon after, Right of Way and Blumhouse helped Chazelle turn fifteen pages of the screenplay into an 18-minute short film. The short film received acclaim after debuting at the 2013 Sundance Film Festival, which attracted investors to produce the complete version of the script. Filming took place in September 2013 throughout Los Angeles over twenty days. The film explores concepts of perfectionism, dedication, and success, and deconstructs the concept of ambition.
